items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. (1) The tier-4 fact is real and is used as evidence: WEB sets an opening curly quotation mark inside web:Ps.118.15 before its second sentence and the closing mark at the end of web:Ps.118.16; the row's observed_substrate_signals #2 offers that quotation-mark structure as a substrate signal with an absence arm ('the voice of rejoicing (v15a) itself carries no quotation mark'), the driver field labels the unit 'A quoted acclamation', and strongest_rejected_alternative rejects the v16 cut as 'what vv15-16 just quoted as communal acclamation' - translation punctuation doing corroboration work and counterevidence-by-absence, barred by the campaign addendum (E-23). (2) It is corroboration, not the resting point, so medium is the right band: the voice contrast stands in the MT bytes with no punctuation layer - oshb:Ps.118.17 carries three 1cs prefix forms, אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה, וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר (byte tier, word indices 1, 3, 4), and oshb:Ps.118.18 two 1cs object suffixes, יִסְּרַ֣נִּי, נְתָנָֽנִי (byte tier), while oshb:Ps.118.15 and oshb:Ps.118.16 carry no first-person form at all; the 'acclamation' reading itself is derivable from oshb:Ps.118.15's own syntax, where ק֤וֹל רִנָּ֬ה וִֽישׁוּעָ֗ה בְּאָהֳלֵ֥י צַדִּיקִ֑ים (byte tier) names a voice and the nominal clause יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל follows as its content. The row's byte claim re-collates: that four-token run stands byte-identically at oshb:Ps.118.15 (word indices 5-8) and oshb:Ps.118.16 (word indices 3-6), and a byte sweep of the run returns exactly those 2 verses. (3) BOTH SIDES of the rival seam at 118:16|118:17 weighed under the book's rules: the preceding unit would close on the doubled clause יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל (second occurrence, oshb:Ps.118.16, byte tier) - a refrain-type close - and the following unit would open לֹֽא אָמ֥וּת (oshb:Ps.118.17, byte tier) on a speaker return to the first person; both are ruled-class signals, so the rival is live on bytes and the row's rejection of it must rest on the byte-grounded voice contrast and on v17 answering vv15-16, never on the quotation marks - which is why the tier-4 lean is a defect and not a stray remark. The row's own edges are sound on ruled classes from both sides: oshb:Ps.118.14 closes in the first person (וַֽיְהִי לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה, byte tier) and oshb:Ps.118.15 opens on the unaddressed communal scene; oshb:Ps.118.18 closes in the first person (נְתָנָֽנִי) and oshb:Ps.118.19 opens on the 2mp imperative פִּתְחוּ (byte tier), coherent with M8-Ps-395 and M8-Ps-397. Ps 118 is an identity psalm (crosswalk); no selah and no K/Q in MT 118:15-18 (pmarks; paseq count-only, 1 at MT 118:15, inventory-cited, single-witness, no seam role); all three Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. (4) Repair validated: the proposed re-grounding on the 1cs distribution is byte-sound and ENDORSED as a field repair (no respan), with two qualifications - name all three v17 forms (the proposal names two) and phrase 'communal' as the row's reading of the voice-clause syntax rather than a byte fact; the WEB quotation mark may remain only as an explicit tier-4 non-evidential disclosure. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_change false, so span_ruling n/a.

Re-swept from bytes with the count object named (the verse's FIRST token, skeleton tier, over verse_map_oshb.json). First token = the masculine demonstrative: 6 verses - MT 24:6, MT 34:7 (= WEB 34:6), MT 49:14 (= WEB 49:13), MT 104:25, MT 118:20, MT 118:24; first token = the feminine demonstrative: 4 verses - MT 109:20, 119:50, 119:56, 132:14; union 10 verses; no further verse-initial token merely begins with either form (prefix-extension check returns the same sets). Under the narrowest reading of the row's object - a verse-initial demonstrative followed by an article-noun as at זֶֽה הַשַּׁ֥עַר (oshb:Ps.118.20) and זֶה הַ֭יּוֹם (oshb:Ps.118.24) - the set is still 3 verses, because oshb:Ps.104.25 opens זֶ֤ה הַיָּ֥ם (byte tier), so the row's 'a book-wide sweep finds it only at 118:20 and 118:24' is byte-false under every reading and carries no digit. Scoped to Psalm 118 the pair is complete (first tokens of MT 118:1-29 swept: the demonstrative heads exactly 118:20 and 118:24), and the row's other demonstrative facts hold: זֹּ֑את stands at word index 3 of oshb:Ps.118.23 after מֵאֵ֣ת יְ֭הוָה הָ֣יְתָה (byte tier), and oshb:Ps.118.22 has no demonstrative. Not load-bearing - the sentence is an anti-driver dampener whose conclusion survives - so medium (E-05 false universal), not high. BOTH SIDES of the row's front seam at 118:21|118:22 weighed: the preceding unit closes on first-person thanksgiving addressed to Yahweh, א֭וֹדְךָ כִּ֣י עֲנִיתָ֑נִי וַתְּהִי לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה (oshb:Ps.118.21, byte tier), and this unit opens on the impersonal third-person saying אֶ֭בֶן מָאֲס֣וּ הַבּוֹנִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.118.22, byte tier) - the explicit speaker/addressee shift is the ruled class that decides, and the verse-initial demonstrative at 118:20 and 118:24 straddles that seam exactly as the row says, so the correction moves no boundary; the rear seam is coherent with M8-Ps-399 (oshb:Ps.118.25 opens on the vocative plea אָנָּ֣א יְ֭הוָה, byte tier). Identity psalm; no selah, no K/Q in MT 118:22-24 (pmarks); all six Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated: both restatements in the proposal are byte-true (psalm-scoped '2 verses'; book-wide 6 masculine / 10 with the feminine form) and are ENDORSED as a field repair, with the qualification that any book-wide digit must name its object, since the article-noun shape alone gives 3 verses (MT 104:25, 118:20, 118:24). Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

Re-swept from bytes with each candidate count object named. The row's form is א֭וֹדְךָ (oshb:Ps.118.21, word index 0, byte tier); its skeleton אודך as a contiguous substring returns 14 verses book-wide - MT 18:50 (= WEB 18:49), 30:13 (= WEB 30:12), 35:18, 43:4, 52:11 (= WEB 52:9), 57:10 (= WEB 57:9), 71:22, 86:12, 108:4 (= WEB 108:3), 118:21, 118:28, 119:7, 138:1, 139:14 - and 12 verses word-bound (the two prefixed tokens at MT 43:4 and 118:28 drop out); at byte tier the pointed token stands in 3 verses (MT 35:18, 118:21, 119:7; accent-stripped 11). The v28 token is וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ (oshb:Ps.118.28, word index 2, byte tier), whose skeleton ואודך sweeps to 2 verses at skeleton tier but to the different set MT 43:4 and 118:28 (byte tier: 118:28 alone) - the toolkit's same-count-different-set trap. No count object yields the row's stated pair, so 'a skeleton sweep of that form returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, Ps.118.21 and Ps.118.28' is byte-false, and it sits beside the book-order neighbor M8-Ps-397's 14-verse digit for the same skeleton (that row names its object loosely as 'the root', but its digit is the substring count), so adjacent rows carry incompatible counts of one form. Not load-bearing: the sentence is a dampener ('not unique to v28') whose direction the correction only strengthens, and the row's seam warrant stands independently - oshb:Ps.118.29 and oshb:Ps.118.1 are byte-equal whole verses of 7 tokens (הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ, byte tier), so the hodu inclusio holds. Identity psalm; no selah, no K/Q in MT 118:28-29 (pmarks); all eleven Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated: the proposal's restated digits (14 substring / 12 word-bound / byte 3 verses at oshb:Ps.35.18, oshb:Ps.118.21, oshb:Ps.119.7; the v28 form's skeleton set oshb:Ps.43.4 and oshb:Ps.118.28) all reproduce and are ENDORSED as a field repair, noting that a byte-tier digit for the v28 form would be 1 verse. both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns no seam - it is a count-object digit inside a dampener - and neither of the row's edges is in question. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

Re-swept from bytes with the count object named. The stanza's light token is וְ֝א֗וֹר (oshb:Ps.119.105, word index 3, byte tier); its bare skeleton אור as a contiguous substring occurs in 0 of the 7 remaining stanza verses MT 119:106-112 (word-bound also 0), and book-wide in 23 verses (8 word-bound), of which the only Ps 119 member is 119:105; the WEB witness agrees - 'light' stands in web:Ps.119.105 alone across web:Ps.119.105-112. So device_notes' 'recurs non-idiomatically at 2 of the stanza's remaining 7 verses (skeleton tier)' is byte-false on every reading, and the same sentence's closing clause ('the paired image itself does not repeat elsewhere in the stanza') already contradicts it. The companion 'lamp' digit survives only as a lexeme count over the attested spellings נֵר (oshb:Ps.119.105) and נֵרִ֑י (oshb:Ps.18.29) - 3 verses, MT 18:29 (= WEB 18:28), 119:105, 132:17 - not as a bare skeleton sweep (substring 12 verses, dominated by false hits such as נרננה; word-bound 2), so its count object is under-named though its digit is defensible; recorded as context, not a new finding. Not load-bearing: the seam warrant is the acrostic, re-verified from bytes (skeleton first letters of MT 119:105-112 are all nun, first seen נֵר (oshb:Ps.119.105); MT 119:113 opens סֵעֲפִ֥ים (oshb:Ps.119.113) on samekh, byte tier), and the recurrence claim sits in texture prose - hence medium (E-05 false digit), not high. Identity psalm; no selah, no K/Q in MT 119:105-112 (pmarks); both Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated: the proposal's measured restatement ('0 of 7') reproduces and is ENDORSED as a field repair, with the qualification that it name the object (skeleton substring of the light token, 0 of 7 verses; WEB 'light', 0 of 7). both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns no seam - a count-object claim in device_notes - and the acrostic seams at 119:104|105 and 119:112|113 are untouched. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

Re-derived from the staged bytes and the inventory. pmarks_Ps.json kq records exactly 1 ketiv/qere note at MT Ps.119.161 (single-witness; none elsewhere in MT 119:161-169), and the staged extract carries the pair as two adjacent tokens at word indices 3 and 4 - the unpointed ketiv ומדבריך followed by the pointed qere וּ֝מִדְּבָרְךָ֗ (oshb:Ps.119.161, byte tier) - while the row's primary driver quote שָׂ֭רִים (oshb:Ps.119.161, word index 0) is a fully pointed token standing outside the pair whose bytes are invariant under either reading. device_notes' claim that 'this row's own primary driver quote above ... follow[s] the unpointed ketiv reading against the pointed qere' is therefore false of the quoted bytes: the driver quote carries neither reading. The clause's other half is true - WEB's plural 'your words' at web:Ps.119.161 follows the plural ketiv against the singular qere - and the row's closing clause is right (the letter identity is unaffected: skeleton first letters of MT 119:161-168 are all shin/sin, first seen שָׂ֭רִים (oshb:Ps.119.161); MT 119:169 opens תִּקְרַ֤ב (oshb:Ps.119.169) on tav, byte tier). The book-order neighbor M8-Ps-420 discloses the same note verse-scoped and correctly, so the corpus carries two incompatible descriptions of one K/Q note. A false mark-attribution claim that is not load-bearing is medium under the severity law, not high; not low because it misstates what the quoted bytes carry rather than merely omitting a disclosure. Identity psalm; no selah in MT 119:161-168 (pmarks); both Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated: the proposal's verse-scoped restatement (one K/Q note at the verse's fourth and fifth tokens; driver quote = the opening word, unaffected; WEB follows the plural ketiv) reproduces from bytes and is ENDORSED as a field repair. both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns no seam - a mark-attribution claim - and the acrostic seams at 119:160|161 and 119:168|169 are untouched. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

Re-derived from bytes both ways under the Ps strategy's own seam law. Ps 127 is a titled identity psalm (crosswalk: 5 WEB / 5 MT verses; the title שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לִשְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה is the prefix of oshb:Ps.127.1, so web:Ps.127.0 = oshb:Ps.127.1 is the right dual-cite). The row's stated warrant for the 127:2|127:3 cut is a topic change plus an absence ('without returning to the house-and-city figures'); strategy section 5 closes tier-1 internal-seam evidence to superscriptions, hallelu-Yah/hodu frames, doxologies, acrostic structure and explicit speaker/addressee shifts, section 6 adds refrain returns, vocative openings and imperative clusters, and the owner addendum bars absence as evidence - a topic change is discussion texture, so the warrant as stated is not of a ruled class, and both observed_substrate_signals describe oshb:Ps.127.1 alone (the paired אִם יְהוָ֤ה clauses and the doubled watch root יִשְׁמָר / שׁוֹמֵֽר, all byte-collated there) and carry no seam signal at 2|3. The auditor's uncited ruled signal re-derives TRUE: לָכֶ֨ם (oshb:Ps.127.2, word index 1, byte tier) is the psalm's only second-person form (no 2ms/2mp suffix or verb stands in MT 127:1, 3, 4 or 5), and oshb:Ps.127.3 opens on the verse-initial presentative הִנֵּ֤ה (14 such verse-initial verses book-wide, skeleton tier) with third-person description. BOTH SIDES weighed: the preceding unit closes on שָׁ֤וְא לָכֶ֨ם מַשְׁכִּ֪ימֵי ק֡וּם ... כֵּ֤ן יִתֵּ֖ן לִֽידִיד֣וֹ שֵׁנָֽא (oshb:Ps.127.2, byte tier) - 2mp address closing on the sleep clause - and the following unit opens הִנֵּ֤ה נַחֲלַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה בָּנִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.127.3, byte tier); the explicit addressee shift is the governing rule that decides, corroborated by the presentative onset. Qualification the repair must carry: the 2mp address is confined to MT 127:2 (1 verse), so an addressee criterion alone would mark 1|2 as readily as 2|3; what fixes the seam at 2|3 is that the repetition שָׁ֤וְא binds vv1-2 (3 tokens in 2 verses: oshb:Ps.127.1 word indices 8 and 17, oshb:Ps.127.2 word index 0; word-bound שוא 10 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) and stops there - absent from MT 127:3-5 - while the presentative onset stands at v3. The seam therefore survives on bytes but not on the row's stated grounds: a defective warrant class with the boundary itself sound is medium, not high; the two-row treatment is permissible under section 6 because the panels are divisible at a ruled-class signal, so no span change is proposed and none is warranted. Ruled coherently with the seam-pair partner M8-Ps-431, whose rejected alternative defers to this row's reason and whose first substrate signal already quotes the הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Ps.127.3) onset: the matching field repair belongs on both rows as one edit (section 10 seam-pair rule). No selah, no K/Q in Ps 127 (pmarks; paseq count-only, 3 at MT 127:1 and 1 at MT 127:2, inventory-cited, single-witness, no seam role); all three Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated and ENDORSED as a field repair with the qualification above (addressee shift plus the שָׁ֤וְא (oshb:Ps.127.2) tie plus the presentative onset; topic change demoted to texture; the signal added to observed_substrate_signals on both rows). Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

Re-measured from verse_map_oshb.json with the objects named (skeleton tier for words and consonant letters; raw codepoints of the staged pointed text for the third). The clause the row names as its object, אָזְנַ֣יִם לָ֭הֶם וְלֹ֣א יַאֲזִ֑ינוּ (oshb:Ps.135.17, word indices 0-3, byte tier), measures 4 words / 17 consonants / 36 codepoints; MT 115:6 as a whole measures 8 / 30 / 67; MT 115:6-115:7 combined 17 / 70 / 156 (155 without a joining space). So as written the claim 'longer than 115:6 alone on all 3 measures ... running shorter only against 115:6-115:7 combined' is false on all three measures and its rider is false too - the clause is shorter than MT 115:6 alone on every measure. The relation holds only when the object is MT 135:17 as a whole verse: 9 / 32 / 70, longer than MT 115:6 on all three and shorter than the combined pair. The row's neighboring claims re-derive TRUE: oshb:Ps.135.16 equals oshb:Ps.115.5 and oshb:Ps.135.18 equals oshb:Ps.115.8 byte-for-byte; oshb:Ps.135.15 and oshb:Ps.115.4 differ even at skeleton tier (עֲצַבֵּ֣י הַ֭גּוֹיִם against עֲֽ֭צַבֵּיהֶם, byte tier); the two verses share their first three tokens at skeleton tier and diverge at the fourth, יַאֲזִ֑ינוּ (oshb:Ps.135.17) against יִשְׁמָ֑עוּ (oshb:Ps.115.6), byte tier. Not load-bearing: the row itself rules the Ps 115 comparison cross-psalm texture, not a seam ground, and its edges rest elsewhere (oshb:Ps.135.15 opens the idol topic on עֲצַבֵּ֣י הַ֭גּוֹיִם after the hinge couplet MT 135:13-14; oshb:Ps.135.19 opens the imperative bless-call בֵּ֣ית יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל בָּרֲכ֣וּ, byte tier), coherent with M8-Ps-445 and M8-Ps-447 - hence medium (E-05 false measure claim), not high. Identity psalms 135 and 115; no selah, no K/Q in MT 135:15-18 or MT 115:4-8 (pmarks); all thirteen Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated: the proposal's whole-verse digits (9 / 32 / 70 against 8 / 30 / 67; combined 17 / 70 / 156) reproduce and are ENDORSED as a field repair, with the qualification that a retained codepoint digit for the combined pair must state its joining convention (156 with one joining space, 155 without). both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns no seam - a measure-object claim inside cross-psalm texture - and both row edges lie outside the finding. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. The tier-4 facts are real: web:Ps.141.7 is set in WEB inside curly double quotation marks with a translator footnote, and the row's confidence sentence locates the obscurity 'in the WEB rendering itself'; MT 141:7 carries no such marking. The row splices no Hebrew and cites no oshb: ref, lists the quotation-mark fact as observed_substrate_signals[1] - an evidence slot - and makes the translation-located sentence its only stated ground for its band, so translation punctuation and a translation-located judgement are doing corroboration work (E-23), not standing as stray remarks; that is medium, not low. Not high, because every seam-bearing claim of the row re-derives from MT under ruled classes: the 3mp chain is byte-real - בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.4, word index 14), בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.5, word index 12), שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Ps.141.6, word index 3), byte tier - and the divine name stands at oshb:Ps.141.1 (יְהוָ֣ה, word index 2), oshb:Ps.141.3 (יְ֭הוָה, word index 1) and oshb:Ps.141.8 (יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י, word indices 2-3) and in no token of MT 141:4-7 (skeleton sweep of the psalm). BOTH SIDES of each seam weighed: at 141:4|141:5 the preceding unit closes on the 2ms jussive petition אַל תַּט (oshb:Ps.141.4, byte tier) running to בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם, and this unit opens יֶֽהֶלְמֵֽנִי צַדִּ֨יק חֶ֡סֶד (oshb:Ps.141.5, byte tier) with no second-person form anywhere in MT 141:5-7 (token lists inspected; the second-person forms of MT 141:1-4 include the imperatives ח֣וּשָׁה, הַאֲזִ֥ינָה (oshb:Ps.141.1), שִׁיתָ֣ה, שָׁמְרָ֣ה, נִ֝צְּרָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.141.3), the jussive תַּט (oshb:Ps.141.4) and the suffixed קְ֭רָאתִיךָ, לָֽךְ (oshb:Ps.141.1) and לְפָנֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Ps.141.2)) - the explicit addressee shift is the ruled class that decides, and it is more precise than the row's 'petition to descriptive report', since oshb:Ps.141.5 still carries prefix forms read as wishes (יֶֽהֶלְמֵֽנִי; the negated jussive אַל יָנִ֣י) but drops the addressee; at 141:7|141:8 this unit closes נִפְזְר֥וּ עֲ֝צָמֵ֗ינוּ לְפִ֣י שְׁאֽוֹל (oshb:Ps.141.7, byte tier, first person plural, no address) and the next opens כִּ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ps.141.8, byte tier) - a vocative opening and addressee return, ruled in section 6; both rulings cohere with M8-Ps-464 and M8-Ps-466. The medium_low band is well placed (sound edges, obscure interior). Titled identity psalm; no selah, no K/Q in Ps 141 (pmarks; paseq count-only, 1 at MT 141:5, inventory-cited, single-witness, no seam role). Repair validated: dropping observed_substrate_signals[1] is endorsed outright; the proposed MT re-anchoring is ENDORSED with qualification - the runs כִּי ע֥וֹד וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.5) and נִשְׁמְט֣וּ בִֽידֵי סֶ֭לַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Ps.141.6) collate at byte tier, but 'unsettled in the Hebrew itself' is an interpretive judgement, not a byte fact, and must be phrased as the row's reading of the clause boundaries and of the subject of נִשְׁמְט֣וּ (oshb:Ps.141.6), while the seam sentence should name the addressee shift rather than a petition-to-report turn. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.
